messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: 25-year-old female
Admission date: [DATE]
Discharge date: [DATE]
Length of stay: [NUMBER] days
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient presented to the emergency department with complaints of acute onset of epigastric pain and nausea with bilious emesis. Initial workup did not demonstrate evidence of biliary or gallbladder pathology. However, her symptoms progressed and she was re-evaluated with a computed tomography that demonstrated a soft tissue mass located posterior to the gallbladder. Further evaluation with magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography observed a complex cystic structure of indeterminate etiology at the porta hepatis.

The patient underwent surgery, during which a hemorrhagic pedunculated mass attached to the infundibulum of the gallbladder was identified and resected. A cholecystectomy was also performed due to inflammation from the hemorrhagic mass. Gross pathology and histology revealed a hemorrhagic benign ectopic liver tissue, and localized cholecystitis in the area adjacent to the mass was also observed.

The patient's postoperative course was uneventful and her symptoms resolved immediately. She was discharged home on the first postoperative day and was asymptomatic when seen in follow-up.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
The patient underwent surgery to remove the hemorrhagic benign ectopic liver tissue and cholecystitis. She was discharged with instructions to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Condition at Discharge:
The patient was asymptomatic and in stable condition at the time of discharge.

Discharge Medications: N/A

Follow-up:
The patient was instructed to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Instructions:
The patient was instructed to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
**Q44**

The principal diagnosis is the ectopic (accessory) liver tissue attached to the gallbladder. It bled, causing the presenting symptoms, and it was the main reason for surgery. Ectopic or accessory liver is a congenital malformation of the liver, coded at Q44.7 (other congenital malformations of liver).

The localised cholecystitis was secondary inflammation caused by the haemorrhagic mass. It would be coded as an additional diagnosis (K81), not the principal one.
